files.content:
--- title: List description: Flat semantic list items with derived numbering. docs: - route: /docs/components/list-toolbar-button title: List Toolbar Button --- List turns supported blocks into flat list items. Kind, marker style, list identity, numbering starts, task state, and indentation are separate fields. ## Features - listType is bulleted, numbered, or task. - listStyle optionally selects a CSS marker. - listId names the list an item belongs to. A list counts on past other blocks, and two lists can interleave. - listLevels holds a list's per-level start and restart rules, as Word stores them. - listStart applies when the item opens its level; listRestart forces the item's number. - checked belongs to task items. - Display ordinals are derived without rewriting following nodes. - Restart numbering and Continue numbering commands. - Markdown rules cover bullets, numbers, and tasks. ## Kit usage ~~~tsx import { ListKit } from '@/components/editor/list'; import { createEditor } from 'platejs/react'; const editor = createEditor({ plugins: [...ListKit], }); ~~~ ## Value ~~~ts const value = [ { type: 'paragraph', listType: 'numbered', listId: 'steps', listStart: 4, indent: 1, children: [{ text: 'Four' }], }, { type: 'paragraph', children: [{ text: 'A note between the steps.' }], }, { type: 'paragraph', listType: 'numbered', listId: 'steps', indent: 1, children: [{ text: 'Five' }], }, { type: 'paragraph', listType: 'task', listId: 'todo', checked: false, indent: 1, children: [{ text: 'Ship it' }], }, ]; ~~~ The third block does not store 5. Plate derives it with editor.read.list.ordinal(at), where `at` is the item's path, node or key; a static renderer that already knows the path passes it. ### Numbering Plate numbers each list on its own, in document order. Blocks of other lists and plain blocks between its items do not end it. A numbered item shows: - its listRestart, when set; - otherwise one more than the list's previous item at its level, while that level is open; - otherwise its listStart, then its level's listLevels start, then 1. Any item of the list closes its deeper levels, so a nested list restarts under each parent. A level's `restartAfter` rule in listLevels changes that. With `0` the level never restarts, and with `n` it restarts only after an item at level `n` or shallower. Each numbered item reads the rule from its own listLevels, and a value at or past its own level acts as the default. Items without listId form their root's default list. Give each list its own id in values that hold more than one list. Commands and typed list markers give a new item an id. It joins a compatible item at its depth before it, otherwise the item it nests under, otherwise a compatible item after it. When none is within 64 blocks, it starts a new list. An item any other edit inserts without an id stays in its root's default list. listStart is latent author intent. Plate keeps it while the item continues its list and applies it when later edits make that item open its level. listRestart forces the number even inside a list. Both fields are signed safe integers, so zero and negative ordered-list starts remain valid. ## Commands ~~~ts import { ListStyle, ListType } from 'platejs'; import { ListPlugin } from 'platejs/react'; const list = editor.plugin(ListPlugin); list.update.toggle({ type: ListType.Bulleted }); list.update.toggle({ type: ListType.Bulleted, listStyle: ListStyle.Square, }); list.update.toggle({ type: ListType.Numbered, listStart: 4, }); list.update.toggle({ type: ListType.Task }); list.update.restart(); list.update.restart({ start: 4 }); list.update.continue(); list.update.outdent(); list.update.clear(); list.update.insert({ type: ListType.Numbered }, { replaceEmpty: true, select: true }); ~~~ `restart` forces the selected numbered item's number, 1 by default. `continue` removes that restart. On the first item of a list, it moves the whole list onto the nearest earlier numbered list at its depth, so the numbers continue it. `clear` removes list fields and indentation from the selected list items without expanding to their unselected siblings. It preserves each block's type and text. Pass `at` to target a location or node selection. `insert` creates a paragraph list item after the current block; `replaceEmpty` replaces an empty source in the same history step. An explicit `at` keeps node-insertion placement, while `after` identifies the block to insert beside. ## HTML and Markdown HTML ul and ol tags map to listType. Explicit CSS list-style-type maps to listStyle. Plate HTML names each item's list with `data-list-id` and its level rules with `data-list-levels`. Each paste or parse gives every source list a fresh id, so a pasted list never joins an unrelated list that shares its id. The first top-level pasted list joins the list it lands in when both lists match in kind, style and heading role. A list that lives only inside a pasted table keeps its own id. In other HTML, each ul or ol is one list. An ol whose start continues the previous ol at its depth joins it, and the first nested list under an item joins that item's list. Word HTML keeps Word's list identity. A list drawn inside its block, such as `

  1. …

` from the static kit, reads back as that block with its list fields, and an item's own `data-list-style` wins over its list's marker. MDAST `list.ordered` maps to `listType`. Each parsed Markdown list gets a new listId, and a start other than 1 parses as `listStart`. The first nested list under an item joins that item's list, and a later nested list under the same item starts its own. When serializing, Plate starts a new Markdown list where the list changes, where items switch between ordered and unordered, or where listStyle changes, so task and bullet items of one list stay one Markdown list. It writes the visible number of each ordered list's first item as its `list.start`, or 1 when the list's numbers would go negative or pass the nine digits CommonMark reads. Markdown cannot carry a forced `listRestart`. It also cannot carry list membership that reads back differently, such as a list that continues past another block; Plate checks membership only for items with a listId. Serialize reports each loss as a `markdown-property-omitted` diagnostic. Markdown parses an item's later paragraphs as blocks without `listType`, one level deeper than the item, and such a block serializes inside the item before it. Task checkboxes map to task `listType` plus `checked`. Inside a GFM table cell, list paragraphs are written as inline `
    `, `
      `, and `
    1. ` HTML, which keeps any start, and read back as lists; see [Markdown](/docs/plate/markdown#table-cells). ## API Reference | API | Purpose | | --- | --- | | ListType | Semantic bulleted, numbered, and task constants. | | ListStyle | CSS marker constants. | | update.toggle(options) | Set or remove list semantics. | | update.restart(options?) | Force the selected numbered item's number; `start` defaults to 1. | | update.continue(options?) | Remove the selected item's restart, or join the list to the previous one from its first item. | | update.outdent(options) | Decrease indentation and clear list fields at the outer level. | | update.clear(options?) | Remove list semantics from the exact selected list items. | | update.insert(input, options?) | Insert a list item with owned construction and placement. | | read.ordinal(at) | Derive a numbered item's display ordinal, or `undefined` when `at` is not a numbered item in the editor's root. |
